mechanismRecords.failureSemantics: Both implementations fail closed to null on tamper/expiry/wrong-secret for their OWN minted tokens (proven for chassis by the fully-read unit test; JOSE's compactVerify/legacy-HMAC path is proven correct under M4's capability-token tests, which reuse the same src/auth/signed-token.ts primitive). DIRECTIONAL CROSS-ACCEPTANCE (verified by source inspection only, not by executing either verifier -- execution is forbidden under this packet's boundary): (a) FORWARD -- src/auth/signed-token.ts verifySignedPayload() branches on `token.split('.').length !== 3` (signed-token.ts:37) to a legacy path verifyLegacyPayload() (lines 18-33) that recomputes `createHmac('sha256', secret).update(payload).digest()` and compares against BOTH base64url and hex encodings of the trailing segment. A chassis-minted token (`base64url(JSON).digest`, 2 segments, digest = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(payload, secret)), plugins/chassis/src/portal-identity.ts:14-17) has exactly this 2-segment shape and exactly this HMAC construction. Under a shared secret, src/auth/portal-identity.ts's verifyPortalIdentity (which calls verifySignedPayload) therefore ACCEPTS a chassis-minted token and returns its claims -- confirmed by matching the legacy fallback's exact comparison logic against chassis's exact mint logic, field for field, without executing either function. (b) REVERSE -- plugins/chassis/src/portal-identity.ts's verifyPortalIdentity splits on `token.lastIndexOf('.')` (portal-identity.ts:20), so for a 3-segment JOSE compact token `header.claimsB64.sig` its 'payload' becomes the JOINED first two segments `header.claimsB64` (containing a literal, non-base64url '.' character partway through). `Buffer.from(payload, 'base64url').toString('utf8')` on that joined string does not decode to a single valid JSON document (it is two base64url segments concatenated with an interior '.' that is not part of the base64url alphabet), so `JSON.parse` throws inside chassis's try/catch (lines 27-30) and verifyPortalIdentity returns null. A JOSE-minted token is therefore REJECTED by the chassis verifier, confirmed by manual JWS Compact Serialization structural analysis (RFC 7515 SS3.1: three base64url segments joined by '.', not decodable as one base64url blob). NET: forward acceptance is real (chassis tokens verify under src/auth, given a shared secret); reverse acceptance fails deterministically at the JSON-parse step (JOSE tokens never verify under chassis). This is a directional compatibility asymmetry, not the blanket 'non-interoperable implementations' characterization in the R1 original return.
